name: open_viewer
title: Open igv-bot
description: Get the Join link that opens igv-bot, an igv.js genome browser, connected to a Room. Use this when the user asks to open a genome browser or says things like "open igv-bot", "open IGV", "launch igv-bot" or "show me the genome browser". A greeting addressed to igv-bot ("hello igv-bot", "hello IGV bot", "hi igv") is also a request to open it: call this tool straight away instead of only greeting back. It opens on hg38 in whole-genome view with the default gene annotation track, or on the genome and locus you pass. A card is shown to the user with an Open igv-bot button. If, and only if, you have the built-in browser of the Claude desktop app (the browser panel beside the conversation), open the Join link in it right away: the page connects to its Room and later tool calls redraw it there. Never use Claude in Chrome or any other browser tool for this; if the built-in browser is not available, do not try anything else. Do not repeat the link or the Room id in your reply. The result of this tool names the Room id: pass it as room on every later igv-bot tool call in this conversation, so the calls reach this igv-bot whichever MCP session they arrive through.

room.description: Only when igv-bot was already opened in this conversation: the Room id from that reply of open_viewer, to get the same igv-bot back, showing what it last showed. Leave it out the first time: igv-bot then opens in a new Room, on the default view.

genome.description: Only when opening a new igv-bot, without room: genome id as on the igv.org genome list, such as "hg19", "mm39" or "hs1", to open on that genome with its default tracks. Leave it out for hg38. For an igv-bot that was already opened, use change_genome instead.

locus.description: Only when opening a new igv-bot, without room: where it opens, as coordinates chr:start-end, a chromosome name, or a gene name such as "MYC". Leave it out for the genome's default view. For an igv-bot that was already opened, use go_to_locus or go_to_gene instead.

name: go_to_locus
title: Go to a locus
description: Move igv-bot to a locus given as coordinates, such as "chr8:127,735,434-127,742,951", or to a whole chromosome, such as "chr8". Use "all" for the whole-genome view. Several loci separated by spaces are shown side by side. For a gene name use go_to_gene. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order.

locus.description: Coordinates as chr:start-end (1-based, commas allowed), a chromosome name, or "all"

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: go_to_gene
title: Go to a gene
description: Move igv-bot to a gene by its name, such as "MYC" or "BRCA1", looked up in the current genome. An unknown gene is reported as an error and the view does not move. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order.

gene.description: Gene name or symbol, such as "MYC"

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: zoom_in
title: Zoom in
description: Zoom igv-bot in by a factor of two, keeping the centre of the view. Call it again to zoom further. The whole-genome view does not zoom: go to a locus or gene first. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order.

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: zoom_out
title: Zoom out
description: Zoom igv-bot out by a factor of two, keeping the centre of the view where possible. Call it again to zoom further. The whole-genome view does not zoom. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order.

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: change_genome
title: Change genome
description: Change igv-bot to another genome assembly, such as "hg19", "mm39" or "hs1" (human T2T). The tracks now loaded are removed and the new genome opens with its own default tracks, at its default view. Only the genomes on the igv.org genome list are available; for one that is not, the reply says so, lists those that are, and igv-bot is left as it was. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order.

genome.description: Genome id as on the igv.org genome list, such as "hg38", "hg19", "mm39" or "hs1"

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: load_tracks
title: Load tracks
description: Load one or several tracks into igv-bot, each from the URL of its file. The URLs come from a reply of search_catalogues (pass the row's url, and its name as the track's name) or from the user, who may give any URL their browser can fetch. Load every track a request asks for in one call: they are shown in the order given, and the Session summary of the reply says where igv.js put them, as a rule above the genome's own annotation track. A track given no name gets igv.js's default, the name of its file. When a loose request matches many tracks in the Catalogues, pick a sensible default, say in one line what you picked, and load it; ask the user only when the candidates differ in a way they would care about. A track that does not load is reported as an error carrying igv.js's own message, as for a file that does not exist or a host that does not permit cross-origin requests; the other tracks of the call are still loaded, and the Session summary shows which. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order.

url.description: The URL of the track's file, such as the url of a search_catalogues row

name.description: The name to show the track under, such as the name of a search_catalogues row. Leave it out for the file's name.

tracks.description: The tracks to load, in the order they are to be shown, top to bottom

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: remove_track
title: Remove a track
description: Remove one track from igv-bot, addressed by its name or by its position in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top: "the second track" is position 2 and "the bottom one" is the last. Give name or position, not both. The user also reorders and removes tracks by hand, so take a position from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A name or position that matches no track is reported as an error listing the tracks, and a name that several tracks share as an error giving their positions; either way nothing is removed. The sequence track cannot be removed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order.

name.description: The name of the track as the Session summary gives it. Case does not matter.

position.description: The position of the track in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: set_track_height
title: Set track height
description: Set the height of one, several or all tracks of igv-bot: to a number of pixels, or "taller" (half as high again) or "shorter" (two thirds as high), so that one undoes the other. A height runs from 1 to 1000 pixels: a number outside that is an error, and taller and shorter stop there. Address the tracks by their names, by their positions in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top, or pass all for every track. Change every track a request means in one call. The user also reorders, resizes and removes tracks by hand, so take positions and heights from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A name or position that matches no track is reported as an error listing the tracks, and a name that several tracks share as an error giving their positions; either way no height is changed. The sequence track keeps its height: all leaves it as it is, and addressing it is an error. The Session summary gives heights in whole pixels. A reply begins with a note when taller or shorter stopped at a limit, or when every track already had the height asked for, so nothing changed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order. When the reply begins with "Note:", the request was carried out other than as asked: tell the person in one sentence of your own what was done and why; otherwise just confirm the change in a few words.

height.description: The height in pixels, from 1 to 1000, or "taller" for 1.5 times the height each track has now, or "shorter" for two thirds of it

names.description: The names of the tracks as the Session summary gives them. Case does not matter.

positions.description: The positions of the tracks in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

all.description: True for every track, in place of names and positions

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: rename_track
title: Rename a track
description: Give one track of igv-bot a new name, the name it is shown under. Address the track by its name or by its position in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top; give name or position, not both, and the new name as newName. The user also reorders and renames tracks by hand, so take a position from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A name or position that matches no track is reported as an error listing the tracks, and a name that several tracks share as an error giving their positions; either way nothing is renamed. The sequence track cannot be renamed. A reply begins with a note when the track already had the new name, so nothing changed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order. When the reply begins with "Note:", the request was carried out other than as asked: tell the person in one sentence of your own what was done and why; otherwise just confirm the change in a few words.

name.description: The name of the track as the Session summary gives it now. Case does not matter.

position.description: The position of the track in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

newName.description: The name to show the track under from now on

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: set_track_color
title: Set track color
description: Set the color of one, several or all tracks of igv-bot, as igv.js's own "Set track color" and "Set alt color" do. color is the color a track is drawn in; altColor is a second color, for the negative values of a wig (signal) track and the minus-strand features of an annotation track. Give either or both, each as "#RRGGBB" or "rgb(R, G, B)": turn a color's name, such as "dark blue", into one of these. "unset" gives a track back the color it was loaded with. Annotation, alignment, variant, wig, interact and shoebox tracks take a color; only wig and annotation tracks take an altColor. Address the tracks by their names, by their positions in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top, or pass all for every track that takes the colors given. Change every track a request means in one call. The user also reorders, recolors and removes tracks by hand, so take positions from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A call is all or nothing: a track named or placed that does not take a color given is an error saying why, and so is a wig track drawn as a heatmap, whose colors are set_signal_style's colorScale; a color that is not one of the forms above is an error too; either way no color is changed. The Session summary gives the colors a track has been given as its options' color and altColor. A reply begins with a note when all passed over tracks that do not take the colors, when a variant track colored by an attribute such as AF is drawn in the one color from then on, or when every track already had the colors, so nothing changed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order. When the reply begins with "Note:", the request was carried out other than as asked: tell the person in one sentence of your own what was done and why; otherwise just confirm the change in a few words.

color.description: The color to draw the tracks in, as "#RRGGBB" or "rgb(R, G, B)", or "unset" for the color each was loaded with

altColor.description: The color of a wig track's negative values or an annotation track's minus-strand features, as "#RRGGBB" or "rgb(R, G, B)", or "unset"

names.description: The names of the tracks as the Session summary gives them. Case does not matter.

positions.description: The positions of the tracks in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

all.description: True for every track that takes the colors given, in place of names and positions

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: set_data_range
title: Set data range
description: Set the data range of one, several or all tracks of igv-bot, as igv.js's own "Set data range", "Autoscale" and "Log scale" do: the values the track's height spans. Give a fixed min and max, or one of them to keep the other as the track has it; or autoscale true for a range that follows what is in view, or false to fix the range the track has now; and logScale, on or off. Give several of these at once, but not a fixed range with autoscale true. Wig (signal), alignment (its coverage), qtl, gwas and gcnv tracks, and interact tracks drawn with proportional arcs, have a data range; only wig and interact tracks have a log scale. Address the tracks by their names, by their positions in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top, or pass all for every track that takes what is given. Change every track a request means in one call. The user also reorders and changes tracks by hand, so take positions from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A call is all or nothing: a track named or placed that has no data range, or no log scale when logScale is given, is an error saying why, and so is a wig track drawn as a heatmap, whose range is set_signal_style's colorScale; a min not below the max is an error too; either way nothing is changed. A fixed range, or autoscale turned off, takes a track out of an autoscale group the user made by hand. The Session summary gives a track's range as its options' min, max, autoscale and logScale. A reply begins with a note when tracks were taken out of an autoscale group, when all passed over tracks that do not take what is given, or when every track already had it, so nothing changed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order. When the reply begins with "Note:", the request was carried out other than as asked: tell the person in one sentence of your own what was done and why; otherwise just confirm the change in a few words.

min.description: The value at the bottom of the tracks

max.description: The value at the top of the tracks

autoscale.description: True for a range that follows what is in view; false to fix the range each track has now

logScale.description: True to draw the values on a log scale, false for a linear one

names.description: The names of the tracks as the Session summary gives them. Case does not matter.

positions.description: The positions of the tracks in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

all.description: True for every track that takes what is given, in place of names and positions

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: set_signal_style
title: Set signal style
description: Set how one, several or all wig (signal) tracks of igv-bot are drawn, as igv.js's own "Graph type", "Windowing function", "Flip y-axis" and "Set color scale" do. graphType draws the values as bar, line, points, heatmap or dynseq: dynseq draws the bases of the sequence at the height of the values, and shows them only below 2 bp per pixel, zoomed in far enough to read the sequence; further out it draws bars. windowFunction is how the values under one pixel are summed up: mean, min, max, or none to draw every value; a track offers those its file does. flipAxis true draws a track upside down, false the right way up. colorScale gives a heatmap its colors: from minColor at min to maxColor at max, or, with a mid, diverging through midColor at the mid; give only what changes, the rest kept as the track has it, and type gradient to drop the mid. Colors are "#RRGGBB" or "rgb(R, G, B)". Give several of these at once. Address the tracks by their names, by their positions in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top, or pass all for every track that takes what is given. Change every track a request means in one call. The user also reorders and changes tracks by hand, so take positions from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A call is all or nothing: a track named or placed that is not a wig track, a colorScale for a track that is not drawn as a heatmap unless graphType heatmap is given with it, a flipAxis for one that is, unless another graphType is given with it, or a windowFunction its file does not offer, is an error saying why; so is a colorScale whose min is not below its max or whose mid is not between them; either way nothing is changed. The color and data range of a heatmap are its colorScale: set_track_color and set_data_range do not apply to it. The Session summary gives a track's style as its options' graphType, windowFunction, flipAxis and colorScale. A reply begins with a note when dynseq will not show at the current zoom, when all passed over tracks that do not take what is given, or when every track already had it, so nothing changed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order. When the reply begins with "Note:", the request was carried out other than as asked: tell the person in one sentence of your own what was done and why; otherwise just confirm the change in a few words.

windowFunction.description: How the values under one pixel are summed up; none draws every value

flipAxis.description: True to draw the tracks upside down, false the right way up

colorScale.description: The colors of tracks drawn as a heatmap: give only what changes

type.description: gradient from min to max, or diverging about a mid. Left out, diverging when a mid is given or the track has one

min.description: The value drawn in minColor, and any below it

mid.description: The value drawn in midColor, between min and max

max.description: The value drawn in maxColor, and any above it

names.description: The names of the tracks as the Session summary gives them. Case does not matter.

positions.description: The positions of the tracks in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

all.description: True for every track that takes what is given, in place of names and positions

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: set_display_mode
title: Set display mode
description: Set how the rows of one, several or all tracks of igv-bot are laid out, as igv.js's own display mode menu does. collapsed draws every feature on one row; squished on rows packed thin; expanded on full-height rows, with labels; full, for an alignment track, gives every read a row of its own, unpacked; fill, for a seg track, stretches its samples to fill the track's height. Annotation and variant tracks offer collapsed, squished and expanded; alignment tracks expanded, squished and full; seg tracks squished, expanded and fill, though a seg track of mutations offers no fill. A wig (signal) track has no display mode: how it is drawn is set_signal_style's graphType. Address the tracks by their names, by their positions in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top, or pass all for every track that offers the mode. Change every track a request means in one call. The user also reorders and changes tracks by hand, so take positions from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A call is all or nothing: a track named or placed that does not offer the mode is an error naming the modes it does, and nothing is changed. The Session summary gives a track's display mode as its options' displayMode; a track without one is expanded, igv.js's default. A reply begins with a note when all passed over tracks that do not offer the mode, or when every track already had it, so nothing changed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order. When the reply begins with "Note:", the request was carried out other than as asked: tell the person in one sentence of your own what was done and why; otherwise just confirm the change in a few words.

mode.description: How the rows are laid out: collapsed, squished and expanded for annotation and variant tracks; expanded, squished and full for alignment tracks; squished, expanded and fill for seg tracks

names.description: The names of the tracks as the Session summary gives them. Case does not matter.

positions.description: The positions of the tracks in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

all.description: True for every track that offers the mode, in place of names and positions

name: set_color_by
title: Set color-by
description: Set what the features of one, several or all tracks of igv-bot are colored by, as igv.js's own "Color by" menus do. An alignment track colors its reads by none, strand (read strand), firstOfPairStrand, pairOrientation, tlen (insert size), unexpectedPair (pair orientation and insert size) or tag, a read tag given as tag, such as HP; the four of paired reads only where its reads are paired. A variant track colors by none or info, an INFO field of its file given as tag, such as AF (allele frequency), VT or SVTYPE. An annotation track of SNPs colors by function or class. Other tracks have no color-by: their color is set_track_color's. Address the tracks by their names, by their positions in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top, or pass all for every track that offers it. Change every track a request means in one call. The user also reorders and changes tracks by hand, so take positions from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A call is all or nothing: a track named or placed that does not offer it is an error naming what it does offer, and nothing is changed. The Session summary gives a track's color-by as its options' colorBy, and a tag or INFO field as colorByTag; an SNP track's is not kept in the Session, and igv.js colors it by function again when it is reloaded. A reply begins with a note when all passed over tracks that do not offer it, or when every track already had it, so nothing changed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order. When the reply begins with "Note:", the request was carried out other than as asked: tell the person in one sentence of your own what was done and why; otherwise just confirm the change in a few words.

by.description: What to color by: none, strand, firstOfPairStrand, pairOrientation, tlen, unexpectedPair or tag for alignment tracks; none or info for variant tracks; function or class for annotation tracks of SNPs

tag.description: With by tag, the read tag to color by, such as HP; with by info, the INFO field, such as AF. Left out otherwise.

names.description: The names of the tracks as the Session summary gives them. Case does not matter.

positions.description: The positions of the tracks in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

all.description: True for every track that offers it, in place of names and positions

name: group_reads
title: Group reads
description: Group the reads of one, several or all alignment tracks of igv-bot, as igv.js's own "Group by" menu does: each group is drawn apart, under its label. Group by none (no grouping), strand (read strand), firstOfPairStrand, pairOrientation, mateChr (chromosome of the mate), chimeric, supplementary (supplementary flag), readOrder or tag, a read tag given as tag, such as RG or HP; the three of paired reads only where the reads are paired. Only alignment tracks have reads to group. Address the tracks by their names, by their positions in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top, or pass all for every alignment track. Change every track a request means in one call. The user also reorders and changes tracks by hand, so take positions from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A call is all or nothing: a track named or placed that is not an alignment track, or whose reads do not offer the grouping, is an error, and nothing is changed. The Session summary gives a track's grouping as its options' groupBy, and a tag as groupByTag; a track without one is not grouped. A reply begins with a note when all passed over tracks that are not alignment tracks, or when every track already had the grouping, so nothing changed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order. When the reply begins with "Note:", the request was carried out other than as asked: tell the person in one sentence of your own what was done and why; otherwise just confirm the change in a few words.

by.description: What to group the reads by: none, strand, firstOfPairStrand, pairOrientation, mateChr, chimeric, supplementary, readOrder or tag

tag.description: With by tag, the read tag to group by, such as RG. Left out otherwise.

names.description: The names of the tracks as the Session summary gives them. Case does not matter.

positions.description: The positions of the tracks in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

name: show_track_parts
title: Show or hide track parts
description: Show or hide the parts of one, several or all tracks of igv-bot, as igv.js's own menus do: true shows a part, false hides it, and a part left out is left as it is. An alignment track's parts are showCoverage, the coverage above its reads, and showAlignments, the reads themselves, never both hidden; viewAsPairs, drawing the two reads of a pair joined on one row, only where its reads are paired and not grouped other than by firstOfPairStrand; and showMismatches, showSoftClips and showInsertions, how its reads are drawn. The alignment track is the one to address for its coverage: the coverage is no track of its own. A variant track's one part is showGenotypes, its samples' rows, where its file has samples. Other tracks have no parts. Address the tracks by their names, by their positions in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top, or pass all for every track that has the parts. Change every track a request means in one call; parts of alignment tracks and genotypes take two calls. The user also reorders and changes tracks by hand, so take positions from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A call is all or nothing: a track named or placed that does not have every part given is an error, and nothing is changed. The Session summary gives a part shown or hidden in the track's options as the tool takes it, where igv.js saves it: a track without one has it as igv.js does unless told, every part shown but viewAsPairs and showSoftClips. A reply begins with a note when all passed over tracks that do not have the parts, or when every track already had them as asked, so nothing changed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order. When the reply begins with "Note:", the request was carried out other than as asked: tell the person in one sentence of your own what was done and why; otherwise just confirm the change in a few words.

showCoverage.description: An alignment track's coverage: true shows it, false hides it

showAlignments.description: An alignment track's reads: true shows them, false hides them, leaving the coverage

viewAsPairs.description: True draws an alignment track's paired reads joined, each pair on one row; false draws each read apart

showMismatches.description: An alignment track's bases that differ from the reference: true colors them, false hides them

showSoftClips.description: An alignment track's soft-clipped bases, at the ends of reads: true shows them, false hides them

showInsertions.description: An alignment track's insertions: true marks them, false hides them

showGenotypes.description: A variant track's genotypes, a row for each sample: true shows them, false hides them

names.description: The names of the tracks as the Session summary gives them. Case does not matter.

positions.description: The positions of the tracks in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

all.description: True for every track that has the parts, in place of names and positions

name: set_visibility_window
title: Set visibility window
description: Set the visibility window of one, several or all tracks of igv-bot, as igv.js's own "Set visibility window" does: the widest view, in base pairs, in which a track's features are loaded and drawn. In a wider view the track shows nothing until the view is zoomed in. A larger window shows features further out but loads more; 0 loads the whole chromosome, which for a large file can be slow. Annotation, variant and alignment tracks have one; other tracks are an error. Address the tracks by their names, by their positions in the tracks of the Session summary, counted from 1 at the top, or pass all for every annotation, variant and alignment track. Change every track a request means in one call. The user also reorders and changes tracks by hand, so take positions from the Session summary of the reply just before, or call read_session_summary first. A call is all or nothing: a track named or placed that has no visibility window is an error, and nothing is changed. The Session summary gives a track's window as its options' visibilityWindow, where igv.js saves one, 0 or less meaning the whole chromosome; an alignment track without one has igv.js's default, 30,000 bp. A reply begins with a note when the window is smaller than the view, so the track shows nothing until it is zoomed in, when all passed over tracks that have no window, or when every track already had it, so nothing changed. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order. When the reply begins with "Note:", the request was carried out other than as asked: tell the person in one sentence of your own what was done and why; otherwise just confirm the change in a few words.

window.description: The widest view, in base pairs, in which the tracks show their features: a whole number, or 0 for the whole chromosome

names.description: The names of the tracks as the Session summary gives them. Case does not matter.

positions.description: The positions of the tracks in the tracks of the Session summary: 1 is the top track

all.description: True for every annotation, variant and alignment track, in place of names and positions

name: set_crosshairs
title: Show or hide the crosshairs
description: Show or hide igv-bot's crosshairs: a vertical and a horizontal line that follow the pointer across the tracks. The Session summary says whether they are showing, as crosshairs; the user also turns them on and off by hand. The whole-genome view has no crosshairs: showing them there is an error, so go to a locus or gene first, and going to the whole-genome view hides them. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order.

show.description: True to show the crosshairs, false to hide them

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: set_centre_line
title: Show or hide the centre line
description: Show or hide igv-bot's centre line: a vertical line marking the middle of the view, the point that zoom_in and zoom_out keep in place. Where several loci are shown side by side, each has its own. The Session summary says whether it is showing, as centreLine; the user also turns it on and off by hand. The whole-genome view has no centre line: showing it there is an error, so go to a locus or gene first, and going to the whole-genome view hides it. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order.

show.description: True to show the centre line, false to hide it

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: set_controls
title: Show or hide the controls
description: Show or hide igv-bot's controls: the navigation bar, and the Shareable URL where igv-bot shows one. The navigation bar is igv.js's own, with its locus box and its buttons; the Shareable URL is in a strip with a copy button. They are hidden and shown together, and start hidden; the genome browser takes the space they leave. The Session summary says whether they are showing, as controls; the user also hides and shows them by hand, with the button above the genome browser. Showing them does not change the view, and the Shareable URL is the same either way. The reply is the resulting Session summary: genome, loci, and tracks in display order.

show.description: True to show the controls, false to hide them

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: read_session_summary
title: Read the Session summary
description: Read what igv-bot is showing now, without changing anything: genome, loci, tracks in display order with name, type, URL and height, and whether the crosshairs, centre line and controls are showing. The user also changes igv-bot by hand (panning, zooming, reordering, resizing or removing tracks) and you are not told when they do. Call this before describing the view or acting on a reference to it, such as "this region" or "the second track", unless a reply from another igv-bot tool has just given you the Session summary.

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: get_shareable_url
title: Get the Shareable URL
description: Get a Shareable URL for what igv-bot is showing now: a link that opens the same genome, loci and tracks in igv-webapp, the IGV web application at igv.org, for anyone the user sends it to. Use this when the user asks for a link to share, send or keep. The link carries the whole Session in itself, so it is long, needs no igv-bot and no Room, and does not expire; it shows the view as it is now, so get a new one after the view changes. Give the user the link exactly as it is in the reply, whole and unshortened. It is not the Join link, which opens igv-bot itself: never give one for the other. The user can copy the same link from igv-bot once the controls are shown. Nothing in igv-bot changes. The reply is the Shareable URL on a line of its own, then the Session summary of the view it opens.

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call.

name: search_catalogues
title: Search the ENCODE and 4DN Catalogues
description: Find tracks for a loose request, such as "CTCF ChIP-seq in K562", in the ENCODE and 4DN Catalogues: the tables of signal, peak and annotation files those projects publish for a genome. Use this whenever the user asks for data by what it is instead of by URL. Both Catalogues are searched at once, for the genome igv-bot is showing. Matching ignores case and punctuation, so "H3K27ac", "h3k27ac" and "H3-K27ac" find the same rows; there are no synonyms, so use the Catalogues' own terms (a cell line as "K562" or "GM12878", an assay as "ChIP-seq" or "DNase-seq"). The reply holds the count of all matching rows, in total and in each Catalogue, and at most 20 of them in full, each with the name and url to load it as a track. When more match than are shown, narrow the search with the filters or with more words. The 4DN rows are the compartments, boundaries and insulation scores of Hi-C experiments: ask for them by outputType. When a loose request matches many tracks, pick a sensible default (for ChIP-seq, a "fold change over control" signal of the replicates together, such as bioRep "1,2"), say in one line what you picked, and load it; ask the user only when the candidates differ in a way they would care about. Hi-C contact matrices and tables of gene or transcript quantifications are never offered: igv-bot cannot show them.

text.description: Free text, such as "CTCF K562". Every word must be somewhere in a row, in any column, so use the few words that name the data and leave out words like "tracks" or "data".

biosample.description: Only rows whose biosample (cell line, tissue or cell type) carries these words, such as "K562" or "liver"

assay.description: Only rows whose assay carries these words, such as "ChIP-seq", "DNase-seq", "RNA-seq" or "Hi-C"

target.description: Only rows whose target (the protein or histone mark of a ChIP-seq experiment) carries these words, such as "CTCF" or "H3K27ac". 4DN rows have no target.

outputType.description: Only rows whose output type carries these words, such as "fold change over control", "signal p-value" or "peaks" in ENCODE, and "compartments", "boundaries" or "insulation score" in 4DN

genome.description: Genome id as on the igv.org genome list, such as "hg38" or "mm10". Leave it out to search for the genome igv-bot is showing, which is nearly always what is wanted.

room.description: The Room id igv-bot was opened with, as given in the reply of open_viewer. Pass it on every call: the search is for the genome that igv-bot is showing.
